messages.text: Littler's bid for historic PDC majors sweep suffers blow

metadata.summary: Luke Littler's bid to qualify for the Players Championship Finals, and keep alive his hopes of claiming a historic clean sweep of PDC major titles in 2026, suffered a blow with a quarter-final exit at PC27.
metadata.content: Luke Littler suffers Players Championship 27 quarter-final exit with loss to eventual winner Jermaine Wattimena | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content Luke Littler suffers Players Championship 27 quarter-final exit with loss to eventual winner Jermaine Wattimena Luke Littler has won every major on PDC circuit so far in 2026 in bid for historic clean sweep; world No 1 must finish in top 64 of Players Championship Order of Merit in order to qualify for Finals in November; 19-year-old lost 6-5 to eventual PC27 winner Jermaine Wattimena in last eight Tuesday 25 August 2026 19:34, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Wattimena hit a 115 checkout to claim his first victory over Luke Littler in the Players Championship 27 quarter-finals (Credit: PDC) Luke Littler's bid to qualify for the Players Championship Finals, and keep alive his hopes of claiming a historic clean sweep of PDC major titles in 2026, suffered a blow with a quarter-final exit at PC27. Littler was beaten 6-5 by Jermaine Wattimena in a final-leg decider, with the Dutchman going on to take the title in Leicester, overcoming countryman Kevin Doets 8-6 in the final. Littler beat Archie Self 6-2, Arno Merk 6-3 and then William O'Connor 6-3 to set up a last-16 tie with Chris Dobey, who he thrashed 6-0, before losing out to eventual champion Wattimena. metadata.summary: Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt.
metadata.content: Tyson Fury fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead in 2026 in America, predicts promoter Frank Warren | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Tyson Fury fight with Anthony Joshua will go ahead in 2026 in America, predicts promoter Frank Warren Talks are ongoing over a possible November blockbuster clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua; an apparent dispute over the location of the fight led to Fury claiming that the event was in "serious doubt" Tuesday 25 August 2026 15:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Boxing promoter Frank Warren says he expects to see the much-anticipated heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in early November but says there are still plenty of negotiations that need to happen first. Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt. Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money".
